sirius-heart.title: シリウスの心臓
sirius-heart.subtitle: Heart of Sirius · self-made MV feat. 异世界情绪
sirius-heart.summary: A self-made MV built around the Sirius binary system, made together with a singer and two modellers.
body: Sirius, the heart of Canis Major, is a binary system of Sirius A and Sirius B. Setting out from the solar system, you listen to the two companions talking in silent space. In their almost eternal orbit they can never meet, because the price of meeting is destruction. Maybe that is the solution of a binary system.

power-still.title: Come Look for Me Down in Hell
power-still.subtitle: Chainsaw Man · Power · still-motion
power-still.summary: A Power still-motion that runs the whole pipeline, starting from cutting figures out of the manga.
body: Work from the first half of the year. Everyone was making Chainsaw Man stills, so I jumped in on impulse — and never expected the workload. Real respect for everyone who finishes one. Power is my favourite character, so I did a few slice-of-life chapters.
Span: from the winter break of my first year to midterms of the spring semester.

I walked through roughly the whole pipeline, starting from cutting figures out of the manga; it really does run on enthusiasm. Time ran out so the second half is parked for later. I clearly cannot tell a story yet and the editing has problems, so I leaned on sound effects to help.

Software: blender.eevee, AE, PS, PR (blender is wonderful — rendering saved me).

procedural-memphis.title: Procedural Memphis
procedural-memphis.subtitle: EXC#1 CM · P6
procedural-memphis.summary: Memphis style in 3D, generated entirely procedurally before geometry nodes existed.
body: Finished 2021-09-21.

Big thanks to 小言 and 崩 for pulling me into a CM collaboration for EXC, where I tried Memphis style in 3D and motion. Made with AE + Blender; Blender had no geometry nodes back then, so every model and 3D animation was generated procedurally with Sverchok and Animation Nodes, while 2D animation and compositing happened in AE. A very interesting piece of work.

diy-renderer.title: DIY Renderer
diy-renderer.subtitle: OpenGL / C++ real-time rendering
diy-renderer.summary: A renderer written from triangle rasterisation up to deferred shading, PBR and screen-space effects — 10k+ lines.
body: I have been writing this renderer for over a year, on and off, and it is past ten thousand lines. Practice really was necessary: I learned a lot and can feel my programming getting noticeably better.

Implemented so far:
- deferred rendering
- PBR materials
- lighting
   - point, directional, spot and area lights
   - hard and soft shadows from shadow maps
- ambient light
- screen-space ambient occlusion
- screen-space reflection
- FXAA (the result is so-so)
I also helped translate a tutorial on area lights; thanks to my classmate @theta-lin for the help.

Early version (2022-01): a very inefficient renderer in C++ — 30 seconds a frame, slower than cycles. Working: triangle rasterisation, z-occlusion, diffuse and ambient terms. Not yet: anti-aliasing, model import, frustum transform, specular, shadow maps. The last image is the eevee reference.

text-island-block.title: Text Island Block
text-island-block.subtitle: AE plug-in
text-island-block.summary: An AE plug-in that grows blocks from text strokes, with extrusion, offset and random exclusion.
body: After a year of C++ I came back to AE plug-in development and it felt much smoother. Scripts that split text into strokes exist, but nothing that generates shapes from those strokes, so I wrote a small plug-in that puts a block under every stroke.

Features: adjustable block colour, blocks-only display, skipping previous effects, hollowing out the counters inside strokes; random extrusion (extruding along two axes rather than scaling), random offset, and excluding blocks in order or at random.
Full walkthrough, examples and download are in the article.

rune-font.title: IsekaiType
rune-font.subtitle: Rune typeface / ornament
rune-font.summary: A hand-made rune typeface: Latin letters, the four Mandarin tones, base-twelve numerals.
body: A while ago (in a fit of chuunibyou) I built a rune typeface that works as a decorative element or an ornament. Only Latin letters, the four Mandarin tones and some punctuation are done; Chinese can be written in pinyin.
Numbers are base twelve, with 10 and 11 written as "#" and "$". Tones: 1st "<", 2nd ">", 3rd "^", 4th "\".
People said it looks like writing from another world, so it is called IsekaiType. Give it a try — the download link is in the pinned comment.
Follow-up (2022-04): because every stroke is its own shape, a stroke-splitting script can pull the strokes apart, which makes handwriting animation with autofill very convenient.

physics-dropper.title: Physics Scatter Script
physics-dropper.subtitle: Blender add-on
physics-dropper.summary: Rather than paying two dollars for an add-on, I wrote a crude physics scattering script.
body: I saw a handy script the other day (physics-dropper on Blender Market) but it costs two dollars, so — in the spirit of writing it myself rather than spending a cent — I made a crude physical scattering script. It sets properties for the dropped objects and the container, starts and ends the drop, applies the transforms and groups the result. It also meant researching add-on development from zero: Blender scripting is a hundred times friendlier than AE, with a low barrier, plenty of tutorials and docs, and easy debugging — about as hard as AE expressions.

blender-patch.title: Blender Curve Radius Patch
blender-patch.subtitle: Curve sculpting #117101
blender-patch.summary: First contribution to Blender: a radius property and interpolation for curve sculpting.
body: My first contribution to Blender.

Someone raised in the issue tracker that curve sculpting had no radius property (#117101), which is inconvenient, so I helped complete that part of the code. The patch (999dfce736) adds a custom initial radius and interpolation from surrounding curve radii, taking radius variation along a curve into account. It should land in 4.1. Next I hope to help with EEVEE-Next.

Walking through an open-source workflow from scratch taught me a lot. Blender has its own chat so communication is easy and the maintainers answer patiently; only the time difference made PR review slow. Maintaining a community this efficiently is impressive.

sdf-field-note.title: Building and Storing SDFs in OpenGL
sdf-field-note.subtitle: Graphics notes
sdf-field-note.summary: Storing a signed distance field in a 3D array and estimating any point with trilinear interpolation.
body: Besides storing a mesh explicitly, geometry can be stored implicitly as the shortest signed distance from any point in space to the surface — a signed distance field.
In practice, for compute and memory reasons, the field is usually kept in a 3D array and any point is estimated quickly with trilinear interpolation.
Full derivation and implementation are in the article.

area-light-note.title: Real-time Area Lights
area-light-note.subtitle: Graphics notes · LTC derivation
area-light-note.summary: Point and directional lights are easy; a continuous emitting surface needs a cleverer real-time solution.
body: Point, directional and spot lights are relatively easy because the source is a point or the direction is constant; an area light emits from a continuous surface, so it needs a fundamentally different approach.

Offline renderers can brute-force it with path tracing (Monte Carlo integration); real time needs something cleverer. This note reproduces and derives the real-time area light solution based on LTC (Linear Transformed Cosines).
The full derivation is in the article.

math-series.title: Maths Series
math-series.subtitle: Itô-isometry / Quadratic Variation / Urysohn's Lemma
math-series.summary: Turning the prettiest theorems from stochastic analysis and topology into images.
body: Itô-isometry — the distance between any two square-integrable processes equals the distance between their Itô integrals: an identity that bridges two spaces elegantly. A record of one of the most beautiful theorems from last term's stochastic analysis.

Quadratic Variation — an operation that only works on stochastic differential equations. Through Itô's lemma it filters out the continuous drift term and keeps only the accumulated variance of the stochastic term; one of the important analytical tools in stochastic analysis.

Urysohn's Lemma — a memento of the last big theorem from my topology course; the proof runs a full three pages. Urysohn constructed, along an almost entirely independent line of thought, a continuous function connecting two closed sets in a T4 space. Intuitively it is the potential between two conductors, or the existence of contour lines between two mountains — though the theorem reaches much further.
These were made last year and I forgot to post them; I plan to finish the maths series.
